**[Epic] Ghost Performance - Platform-wide ghost-induced slowness**

This epic tracks all ERE escalations and Aha tickets related to ghost performance. Impact: enduser, forward, and origin slowness across the Akamai network that is agnostic to customer, ARL, or config (affects all customers on the platform), including slowness from crypto operations in ghost or the crypto network. Root cause: not yet isolated; this is an umbrella epic for individual investigations. Resolution status: In Progress / Unresolved, with workarounds applied per incident. Prevention: prioritize the linked Aha performance fixes and track ghost latency regressions. No linked ERE tickets are currently attached at the epic level.

**[Epic] Ghost Availability - Ghost rolls, crashes and 5xx availability issues**

Umbrella epic for ERE escalations and Aha tickets covering ghost availability problems: ghost/memory rolls, ghost and kernel crashes, ghost serving 5xx to end users while not heavily loaded, and SSL handshake failures between Edge/TD0/TD1. Impact: end-user availability degradation and elevated 5xx/handshake failures. Root cause: tracked per individual incident; not defined at the epic level. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Prevention: drive resolution of the underlying availability fixes and monitor roll/suspension and handshake-failure metrics. No linked ERE tickets at the epic level.

**[Epic] Mapping Availability - Region overload and wrong DNS responses**

Umbrella epic for mapping-availability escalations: regions overloaded by spiky traffic, mapper concentrating load on a few regions despite available platform capacity, overload from Sureroute or other uncontrolled traffic, wrong DNS records served to end users, and mapping configs that cause errors. Impact: availability degradation and errors served to end users. Root cause: per-incident (load concentration, DNS/config errors). Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Prevention: improve mapper load balancing, validate DNS records, and audit mapping configuration. No linked ERE tickets at the epic level.

**[Epic] Mapping Performance - Sub-optimal mapping and pingpoint issues**

Umbrella epic for mapping-performance escalations: pingpoint issues, capacity available but inefficiently used by the mapper, bad ping scores unrelated to capacity or real network loss, and degraded performance from outdated or manually introduced mapping configurations. Impact: sub-optimal routing and slower end-user performance. Root cause: per-incident mapping inefficiencies and stale configs. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Prevention: tune mapping components, remove manual/stale configs, and investigate pingpoint scoring. No linked ERE tickets at the epic level.

**[Epic] Mapping Maps Limitations - Missing regions on Edge/TD0/TD1 maps**

Umbrella epic for performance issues caused by the maps used for mapping: Edge/TD0/TD1 maps missing regions, and regions that have platform capacity but are not included in the maps. Impact: traffic not directed to available nearby capacity, degrading performance. Root cause: map composition gaps rather than platform capacity shortfalls. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Prevention: audit and update map region membership so available capacity is represented. No linked ERE tickets at the epic level.

**[Epic] Network Capacity Issues - Capacity limitations and server overload**

Umbrella epic for capacity-related escalations: customer escalations due to capacity limitation, server overload from lack of capacity, and inter-continental traffic with no ICN or insufficient ICN capacity. Impact: server overload and degraded inter-continental delivery. Root cause: insufficient or poorly distributed network capacity. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Prevention: capacity build-out, ICN provisioning, and traffic-flow optimization tracked via the linked Aha/PERFREL work. No linked ERE tickets at the epic level.

**[Epic] ARL/Platform Configuration Issues - Customer-specific config problems**

Umbrella epic for escalations limited to an individual customer or ARL rather than the whole platform: performance/availability problems from customer configuration, not following product best practices, using the wrong map for the wrong traffic, and requests to raise platform default limits (e.g., request header size, ESI file size). Impact: localized customer performance/availability degradation. Root cause: misconfiguration and best-practice gaps. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Prevention: enforce best practices, correct map usage, and review limit-increase requests. No linked ERE tickets at the epic level.

**[Epic] Customer/Platform Review - Event readiness and best-practice reviews**

Umbrella epic for proactive review escalations: event review/readiness for customers, best-practice requests, and platform review during install checklisting. Impact: preventive rather than incident-driven; aims to avoid future performance/availability issues. Root cause: not applicable (proactive review work). Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Prevention: standardize event-readiness and install-checklist review processes. No linked ERE tickets at the epic level.

**[Epic] Third-Party/Origin Issues - Problems outside Akamai's control**

Umbrella epic for escalations rooted in third parties or customer origins: customer impact caused by origin behavior, certificate issues from customers not following best practices, and other factors outside Akamai's control. Impact: customer-facing degradation that does not originate from the Akamai platform. Root cause: external origin/third-party and customer-side configuration. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Prevention: educate customers on origin and certificate best practices and improve detection/attribution. No linked ERE tickets at the epic level.

**[Epic] Visibility Issues - Hard-to-debug incidents from missing telemetry**

Umbrella epic for escalations that are difficult to debug due to lack of visibility: wrong logging of information, issues hard to debug from inadequate logging, and load reporting that is missing or reported against the wrong map. Impact: slower diagnosis and resolution of incidents. Root cause: insufficient/incorrect logging and load reporting. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Prevention: improve logging coverage and accuracy and fix load-reporting attribution. No linked ERE tickets at the epic level.

**[Epic] Wrong Escalation - Incorrectly routed ERE escalations**

Umbrella epic for tickets wrongly escalated to ERE: issues escalated without involving Akatech, and issues escalated to ERE that are not actually handled by ERE. Impact: wasted triage effort and delayed routing to the correct owner. Root cause: process/routing gaps and miscommunication. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Prevention: clarify escalation criteria and routing, and audit misrouted tickets (consolidated under ERECSO-31). No linked ERE tickets at the epic level.

**[Story] Visibility for Origin Traffic - No 5xx breakdown between platform vs origin**

The Akamai platform lacks a breakdown of failed (5xx) requests, so it cannot separate failures caused by the platform from failures arriving from the origin; last-mile visibility of Akamai-caused errors at the Edge is also missing. Impact: customer issues cannot be cleanly distinguished from Akamai issues, hampering failover policies and end-user performance. Root cause: missing telemetry/instrumentation (5xx attribution). Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Linked tickets: PERFREL-306 (dependency) plus ERE-486, ERE-1402, ERE-638, ERE-1070, ERE-474 (escalations driving the ask). Prevention: add the missing edge/forward 5xx visibility.

**[Story] Cryptoserver Performance - Poor cryptoserver mapping and coverage (Resolved)**

~70% of FF and ~45% of ESSL hostnames don't use Pconn, so every request does a DNS lookup and SSL handshake; the edge also fails to map to the nearest cryptoserver, causing 2-3x cryptoserver latency, and cryptoserver capacity is missing in some major MLE locations. Impact: elevated SSL handshake latency for affected products. Root cause: sub-optimal cryptoserver mapping and limited deployment. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - folded into the Cryptoserver performance outcome (Li-Wei's group). Linked tickets: PERFREL-324 (dependency), ERE-525 (escalation). Prevention: improve cryptoserver mapping and widen deployment near large MLEs.

**[Story] KRP Impact on Handshake Performance - Keysign throttling degrades SSL (Resolved)**

Many ESSL customers do not use persistent connections; when a slot sees many keysigning requests, KRP (Keysign Robustness Protection) engages and SSL handshake performance degrades. Goal was to quantify how often KRP triggers, which customers are affected, and how to reduce impact. Impact: degraded handshake performance for non-Pconn ESSL customers. Root cause: KRP throttling under high keysign load. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations or repeat patterns in 2025; remaining actions handled as KTLO. Linked ticket: ERE-550 (escalation). Prevention: promote persistent connections and monitor KRP activation.

**[Story] Improve In-Metro Mapping - Reduce out-of-metro routing (Resolved)**

~15-40% of traffic maps out-of-metro because nameserver locality is broken (e.g., a single nameserver marked local to all US regions), so edge scoring cannot prefer truly local regions. Impact: higher edge RTT and worse throughput/transfer times. Root cause: incorrect locality/proximity relationships in maps. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations or repeat patterns in 2025; addressed as KTLO. Linked tickets: PERFREL-221 (dependency) plus ERE-568, ERE-601, ERE-1197 and ANREACT-32 (escalations). Prevention: fix nameserver-to-region locality and add auditable per-continent locality rules.

**[Story] Metrocache as Replacement for TD0 Maps - Distributed caching adoption (Resolved)**

Moves the modernized Metrocache (MCH) distributed caching/offload model from experimental rollout to limited global availability, including install-base adoption of small/medium CacheH maps, deprecation/folding-in of PCH, turnkey enablement for new customers, and health-monitoring tooling. Impact: improved, more consistent tier offload, reduced manual map intervention, and better edge load-sharing. Root cause: not applicable (platform improvement initiative). Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations or repeat patterns in 2025; KTLO. Linked tickets: PERFREL-304 (dependency), ERE-554, ERE-1823 (escalations). Prevention: continue phased MCH adoption and offload monitoring.

**[Story] Map Coverage to Avoid OOC - Edge/TD/SS maps missing regions (Resolved)**

ERE received many escalations where Edge/TD/SS maps were missing regions within a country, forcing out-of-country (OOC) mapping; the goal was to update maps (including auto-updating SS maps as they near capacity) rather than have customers escalate. Impact: OOC mapping causing performance degradation. Root cause: map region coverage gaps, not platform capacity. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations or repeat patterns in 2025; KTLO. Linked tickets: a large set of ERE escalations (e.g., ERE-557, ERE-654, ERE-1110, ERE-1218) plus outward ERE-1339. Prevention: proactively maintain map coverage and SS allowlists.

**[Story] Mapper Region Overloading - Regions driven beyond soft cap**

Many escalations involve the mapper overloading regions/links beyond the region soft cap, causing ghost rolls and 5xx, during large events, spiky traffic, slow rebalancing of non-load-balanced load, high flit/manifest traffic, multiple high-flit streams on one region, or spiky Sureroute traffic. Impact: region overload, ghost rolls, and 5xx affecting co-located customers. Root cause: mapper not preventing/relieving overload fast enough; FOM-lowering workaround does not scale. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround (manual FOM adjustment) in use. Prevention: build scalable overload-prevention; treat as an epic of related fixes. No linked ERE tickets attached.

**[Story] Platform Instability from Ghost Rolls/Self-Suspensions (Resolved)**

Customer escalations tie back to ghost rolls (memtotals, asserts) and self-suspensions, which degrade performance/reliability via SSL handshake failures and high connection-establishment times before ghost accepts connections; impact is severe for products relying on a small set of healthy regions (e.g., API-X). Impact: reliability and performance degradation of end-user traffic. Root cause: ghost roll/suspension instability. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations or repeat patterns in 2025; KTLO. Linked tickets: PERFREL-332 (dependency), ERE-584 (escalation). Prevention: reduce roll/suspension frequency and protect critical regions.

**[Story] Server-Side Visibility into SSL Slowness - mdpc logging gaps (Resolved)**

Server-side SSL handshake visibility is insufficient: the 'mdpc' variable meant to log metadata-load slowness on SNI slots is unreliable (no logging seen in ESSL r-lines) and disabled on Freeflow. Evidence shows a strong correlation between metadata file size and handshake time (reducing metadata cut handshake times 20-50%). Impact: inability to diagnose metadata-driven SSL slowness. Root cause: broken/disabled mdpc logging. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations or repeat patterns in 2025; KTLO. Linked tickets: ERE-559, ERE-606 (escalations). Prevention: fix mdpc logging and reduce metadata size.

**[Story] Incorrect Load Reporting - Unassigned load the mapper can't move (Resolved)**

End-user traffic is not reported in several scenarios - multi-CDN hostnames that don't resolve to Akamai, edge hostnames with Zone Access Mapping (ZAM) enabled, and Sureroute load reported on the RA map - so this traffic becomes unassigned load that the mapper cannot rebalance. Impact: impaired load balancing and region management. Root cause: gaps in load reporting/attribution. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - continued tracking moved to ERECSO-69. Linked tickets: ERE-632, ERE-653, ERE-655 (escalations). Prevention: fix reporting outside customer ARL data so all load is assignable.

**[Story] Content Corruption Impacting Customers - VPF/VSF corruption (Resolved)**

Several incidents of content corruption impacted Video Publisher/Streaming flows (VPF/VSF), notably Disney (2020) and Hulu (2022). Impact: corrupted content delivered to customers, a high-severity delivery-quality issue. Root cause: per-incident corruption in the delivery path (tracked via Aha DEL-222). Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations or repeat patterns in 2025; KTLO. Linked tickets: PERFREL-351 (dependency) plus ERE-1303, ERE-1137, ERE-1304, ERE-1027, ERE-999, ERE-1012 (escalations). Prevention: corruption detection/guards in the edge delivery path.

**[Story] Product Best Practices Not Followed - Best-practice gap escalations (Resolved)**

Category ticket capturing all ERE escalations where product best practices were not followed by customers/teams. Impact: avoidable performance/availability issues caused by non-adherence to recommended configuration. Root cause: best-practice and enablement gaps. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - scope expanded into and consolidated under ERECSO-31. Linked tickets: a large set of ERE escalations (e.g., ERE-799, ERE-1071, ERE-1245, ERE-1590) plus automation/linked relationships. Prevention: best-practice enforcement, customer education, and auditing under the consolidated ERECSO-31 effort.

**[Story] Wrong Map for Wrong Traffic - Customer using incorrect product map**

Category ticket for issues caused by a customer using the wrong product map (Edge, TD0, or TD1) for their traffic type. Impact: performance/availability degradation from mismatched map selection. Root cause: incorrect map configuration on the customer. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Linked tickets: ERE-2584, ERE-1079 (escalations). Prevention: validate map-to-traffic suitability during onboarding/reviews and correct misconfigured maps.

**[Story] Increasing Platform Default Limits - Limit-increase requests (Resolved)**

Category ticket capturing ERE requests to increase platform default limits for specific customers. Impact: customers blocked by default limits until reviewed/raised. Root cause: default platform limits insufficient for certain customer use cases. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations or repeat patterns in 2025; KTLO. Linked ticket: ERE-2282 (escalation). Prevention: document limit-increase criteria and review process.

**[Story] KB Article Not Followed - Diagnosis/process gaps (Resolved)**

Category ticket for escalations created because a Knowledge Base article was not followed correctly, leading to individual customer impact or improper diagnosis. Impact: avoidable customer impact and toil from incorrect handling. Root cause: KB adherence and diagnostic-process gaps. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - scope folded into ERECSO-31 (closed per Dec 8 meeting; can be reopened if a clear pattern emerges). Linked tickets: multiple ERE escalations (e.g., ERE-1060, ERE-1129, ERE-2219). Prevention: improve KB usage and diagnostic rigor under ERECSO-31.

**[Story] Individual Customer/ARL Issues - Localized, non-platform-wide problems**

Category ticket for issues limited to an individual customer or ARL that do not impact all customers on the platform. Impact: localized customer performance/availability problems. Root cause: per-incident, customer/ARL-specific. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Linked tickets: a large set of ERE escalations (e.g., ERE-863, ERE-880, ERE-1139, ERE-1160) plus linked issues. Prevention: track recurring per-customer patterns and feed systemic fixes back to the relevant epics.

**[Story] Insufficient Information in ERE Tickets - Ticket-quality gaps (Resolved)**

Category ticket for escalations to ERE that did not meet ticket-quality standards (insufficient data points, lack of detailed investigation by the requestor). Impact: added triage toil and slower resolution. Root cause: incomplete escalation submissions. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - consolidated under ERECSO-31. Linked tickets: multiple ERE escalations (e.g., ERE-1202, ERE-2628, ERE-2937, ERE-2964). Prevention: enforce escalation templates/quality gates via the ERECSO-31 audit.

**[Story] Audit ERE Escalations - Consolidated process-quality epic**

Consolidation epic (Aha TOIL-I-46) auditing escalation quality: incorrect ticket routing (should go to another team), insufficient information (ERECSO-30), KB articles not followed (ERECSO-28), and product best practices not followed (ERECSO-24). Impact: reduced toil and faster, correctly-routed resolutions. Root cause: process, routing, and enablement gaps across escalations. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Linked tickets: a very large set of ERE escalations plus automation/linked/relates relationships (e.g., ERE-3071, ERE-1311, ERE-1372). Prevention: standardized routing rules, quality gates, and best-practice/KB enforcement.

**[Story] Questions/Review of Platform Limits - Limit inquiries (Resolved)**

Category ticket for ERE tickets that ask questions about or request review of platform limits. Impact: low-severity informational/review workload rather than active incidents. Root cause: not applicable (review/inquiry). Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations or repeat patterns in 2025; KTLO. Linked ticket: ERE-1029 (escalation). Prevention: publish clear platform-limit documentation to reduce repeat inquiries.

**[Story] Issues During Software Install Checklisting - Pre-deploy findings (Resolved)**

Category ticket for ERE tickets created during platform checklisting at software install time. Impact: issues caught proactively before/at deployment rather than customer-facing incidents. Root cause: configuration/readiness gaps surfaced during checklisting. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations or repeat patterns in 2025; KTLO. Linked tickets: many ERE escalations (e.g., ERE-2869, ERE-2882, ERE-1354, ERE-1534) plus relates links. Prevention: strengthen install checklists to catch these earlier.

**[Story] Baseline Push - Feature Rollout Rollbacks**

Tracks baseline/delivery product rollout changes that had to be rolled back due to issues found during checklisting or after rollout. Impact: rollout disruption and rework when changes regress. Root cause: defects/regressions surfaced during or after baseline pushes. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Prevention: strengthen pre-rollout validation and staged rollout/rollback procedures. No linked ERE tickets attached.

**[Story] Customer Event Review - Web/Media event-readiness reviews**

Category ticket (Aha MD-I-15) for event reviews of customer configs, split across Web and Media. Web: Edge-map suggestions (esp. when API-X recommended) and FOM adjustments on top regions. Media: TD0 map suggestions, capacity reviews with map-ops for large events (SuperBowl, IPL, new launches like Max/D+), Ad-delivery reviews, cascading-timeout tuning, and FA/QR resiliency settings. Impact: proactive performance/capacity assurance for high-profile events. Root cause: not applicable (proactive review). Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Linked tickets: ERE escalations (e.g., ERE-1745, ERE-1312, ERE-1774, ERE-2472). Prevention: standardize event-readiness playbooks.

**[Story] Anycast Origin Support for Sureroute - SR doesn't support anycast origins by default**

The current SureRoute (SR) implementation does not support anycast origins by default. Impact: customers with anycast origins cannot use SR cleanly out of the box. Root cause: SR design limitation around anycast origin handling. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved. Workaround: build a custom map that includes regions from all locations where the anycast origin is advertised (per the SureRouteMapMaker FAQ and Akatec KB). Linked ticket: ERE-1042 (escalation). Prevention: add native anycast-origin support to SR (Aha COREPERF-45).

**[Story] Origin Not RFC-Compliant for HTTP/H2 - Customer origin behavior degrades end users (Resolved)**

Category ticket for issues caused by customer origins that are not compliant with the HTTP/H2 RFCs, leading to end-user performance problems. Impact: end-user performance degradation rooted in customer-side (non-Akamai) behavior. Root cause: origin RFC non-compliance. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations or repeat patterns in 2025; handled as KTLO. Linked ticket: ERE-1109 (escalation). Prevention: detect/flag non-compliant origins and guide customers to RFC-compliant configuration.

**[Story] FPJ Design Issues - Jetstream/fast-purge defects cause stale content and 5xx (Resolved)**

Ghost FPJ (Jetstream) design has several issues causing stale content, purge-sequence errors, or feature incompatibilities: slow purge-history catch-up (GHOST-1012), store-entry sequence restoration after ghost restart causing cache invalidation/extra origin hits (PURGE-I-6), 5xx on purge validation (GHOST-534), CacheTag/QR incompatibility (WEBGESC-314), and lazy content-tag purge compaction that can exceed memory limits and serve stale metadata after a roll. Impact: stale content, increased origin load, and 5xx. Root cause: FPJ design/implementation gaps. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations in 2025; KTLO. Optimizations tracked under GHOST-532. Linked tickets: many ERE escalations (e.g., ERE-709, ERE-1115, ERE-950, ERE-462). Prevention: deliver the FPJ enhancement epic.

**[Story] H2 Write Timeout after 10s causing RESET to Clients (Resolved)**

Multiple escalations showed CLIENT_ABORT in logs and an RST packet from Akamai, with ghost transfer_time of 10s; analysis showed this happens when ghost fails to write 1KB to the socket within 10s (slow clients). Impact: client aborts/resets and failed transfers for slow clients. Root cause: a 10s H2 write timeout that is too aggressive. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations in 2025; KTLO. Linked tickets: GREL-1535, GHOST-4009, PERFREL-349, GHOST-3440 (dependencies/fixes) plus ERE-2208, ERE-972, ERE-1145, ERE-1700, ERE-942, ERE-2776 (escalations). Prevention: raise the write-timeout default and root-cause the slow-write condition.

**[Story] Network Capacity Issues Causing Perf Degradation - OOC mapping from lack of in-country capacity**

Category ticket for capacity issues that caused out-of-country (OOC) mapping due to a lack of in-country capacity. Impact: degraded performance when traffic must be served from another country. Root cause: insufficient in-country network capacity. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Linked tickets: ERE-3175, ERE-3124, ERE-3189 (escalations). Prevention: targeted in-country capacity build-out.

**[Epic] Platform Availability and Performance - Non-ghost, non-mapper platform issues**

Umbrella epic for all ERE escalations related to platform availability that are NOT ghost or mapper, plus the Aha tickets meant to resolve them (covers other platform components). Impact: platform availability/performance degradation from miscellaneous components. Root cause: tracked per-incident across non-ghost/non-mapper components. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Prevention: drive the linked component-level fixes. No linked ERE tickets at the epic level.

**[Story] KMI Availability Issues - Key Management Infrastructure availability (Resolved)**

Category ticket for platform availability issues caused by KMI (Key Management Infrastructure). Impact: availability degradation tied to KMI. Root cause: per-incident KMI availability problems. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations or repeat patterns in 2025; KTLO. Linked tickets: ERE-1376, ERE-1153 (escalations). Prevention: harden KMI availability and monitoring.

**[Story] Mapping Pingpoint Issues - Bad pingpoint degrades mapping**

Mapping-performance escalations where the root cause was bad pingpoint (PP). Key patterns: low-load but customer-critical ASNs lacking PP; some PPs with higher latency/poor routing vs. others in the same ASN (ISP-specific cases in ERECSO-63); the 'poor PP' designation logic (100% loss to all ecors) is sub-optimal and can keep picking far regions while in-country regions suffer loss; a bug where the mapper randomly picks among manual PPs when some go unpingable; and slow (6-8h) recovery from bad PP. Impact: degraded routing/performance. Root cause: PP selection/scoring and recovery gaps; limited debugging visibility. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Linked tickets: many ERE escalations (e.g., ERE-1130, ERE-1451, ERE-1687, ERE-1483). Prevention: improve PP scoring, faster recovery, and PP debug tooling (Aha MD-I-46).

**[Story] Ghost Rolls Caused by Software Issues - Roll codes 256/259 (Resolved)**

Tracks ghost rolls with roll codes 256/259 caused by software issues that led to customer impact/escalations. Impact: ghost rolls degrading availability/performance for affected customers. Root cause: software defects triggering rolls. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations or repeat patterns in 2025; KTLO. Linked tickets: a large set of ERE escalations (e.g., ERE-470, ERE-590, ERE-1586, ERE-2925) plus related ERE-3018/3076/3149/3155/3222. Prevention: fix the underlying software roll triggers and monitor roll codes 256/259.

**[Story] Ghost Rolls from Traffic - Memtotals/self-suspensions (roll code 257) (Resolved)**

Tracks customer escalations due to memtotal rolls (roll code 257) or rolls caused by high traffic volume on certain regions leading to self-suspensions. Impact: region instability, ghost rolls, and self-suspensions affecting co-located customers. Root cause: high/spiky traffic driving memory rolls and suspensions. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations or repeat patterns in 2025; KTLO. Priority: High. Linked tickets: many ERE escalations (e.g., ERE-2041, ERE-2272, ERE-1217, ERE-555, ERE-588). Prevention: improve overload/roll protection and region load balancing.

**[Story] SSL Handshake Failure Issues - Track and reduce SSL HS failure rate**

Tracks all SSL handshake (HS) customer escalations and ties them to platform SSL-HS-failure-rate improvements via added visibility, debugging capability, root-cause analysis, and ultimately fixes. Impact: SSL handshake failures affecting end users. Root cause: multiple per-incident causes; limited HS visibility hampers diagnosis. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Linked tickets: ERE-950, ERE-1152, ERE-1329, ERE-398, ERE-2336, ERE-1337, ERE-1539, ERE-933 (escalations). Prevention: improve HS telemetry and drive failure-rate-reduction fixes (Aha COREREL-I-27).

**[Story] Region Overload from Large/Spiky Traffic on Single/Multiple Regions**

Tracks issues caused by large or spiky traffic on one or more regions (e.g., high-flit API traffic causing region overloads, or high incoming requests not spread optimally in-region), often requiring FOM-adjustment and load-spreading workarounds. Impact: region overloads degrading performance/availability. Root cause: traffic spikes/concentration exceeding region capacity and sub-optimal in-region spreading. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround (FOM adjustment, load spreading) in use. Priority: High. Linked tickets: a very large set of ERE escalations (e.g., ERE-509, ERE-1272, ERE-2471, ERE-2448). Prevention: scalable overload prevention (Aha COREPERF-E-26).

**[Story] Mapper Causing Overloaded Links - Mapper can't move traffic optimally (Resolved)**

Tracks overloaded-link issues caused by the mapper being unable to move traffic around optimally. Impact: link overloads degrading delivery. Root cause: mapper load-balancing limitations. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations or repeat patterns in 2025; KTLO. Linked tickets: ERE-1894 (escalation), ERE-1512 (linked). Prevention: improve mapper traffic-movement/load-balancing logic.

**[Story] Midgress Region Overload from SR/SS Traffic**

Tracks region overloads from SureRoute (SR)/SiteShield (SS) traffic spikes. Themes: (1) SR co-existing with edge/TD traffic concentrates excessive last-hop traffic with slow rebalancing, causing localized overloads; (2) SS overloads, often from custom/stale SS maps concentrating traffic on few regions (in-region machine imbalance tracked in ERECSO-67). Impact: midgress region instability. Root cause: SR last-hop load balancing not aggressive enough and degraded SS maps; no way to selectively suspend SR traffic from a region. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Linked tickets: ERE-629, ERE-648, ERE-1288, ERE-2673 plus MAPPINGENG-7827. Prevention: improve SR last-hop load balancing (score quantization) and SS map maintenance.

**[Story] Proactive Customer Load Test Reviews (Resolved)**

Tracks issues related to customer load testing. Impact: load tests (often from concentrated cloud agents) can overload regions if not reviewed. Root cause: load-test traffic profiles and process gaps. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - resolved by updating the web load-test guidelines doc (ac-aloha web-load-test-guidelines), which reduced overall load-test requests. Linked tickets: ERE-1611, ERE-1459, ERE-1826 (escalations). Prevention: maintain and enforce the load-test guidelines.

**[Story] Region Overload from Large MPGs - Fractional Assignment insufficient**

Regions get overwhelmed by sudden influx of traffic from large MPGs (Mapping Groups), especially cloud-provider demand (AWS, GCP) with fewer-but-larger MPGs, and some end-user ASNs (Korea, Vietnam); worse for web/api maps with short-lived high-f2b traffic and for concentrated cloud-agent load tests. Impact: server/region overloads. Root cause: Fractional Assignment doesn't help when demand exceeds the 3-region limit or uFMP safeties force fallback; topology.xml maintenance is manual/reactive. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Labels: PSGTopIssue. Linked tickets: many ERE escalations (e.g., ERE-1031, ERE-2296, ERE-2842, ERE-2686). **[Story] Single-Customer Issues Related to FSS (Forward Serial Selection)**

Tracks degradation where FSS was not enabled or the default FSS was insufficient. Web: no explicit forward FSS - cacheable/query-tag requests would benefit from FSS to spread footprint/hits and avoid machine overload under high f2h (risk: lower pconn). Media (AMD/DD): FSS on by default, but manifests/SSAI with a static base URL (AK_PATH) may need extra hashing on Ghost IP to avoid parent/CW overload; selectable via Property Manager. Other cases: incorrect integration or insufficient FSS range (e.g., sharded PCH maps). Impact: machine/parent overload and uneven offload. Root cause: missing/insufficient FSS configuration. Resolution status: In Progress / Unresolved, workaround available. Linked tickets: many ERE escalations (e.g., ERE-2589, ERE-1362, ERE-2728) plus DPEREQ-313/315. Prevention: tune FSS defaults/ranges per product use case (Aha MD-I-20).

**[Story] Single-Customer Issues Related to Fail-Action / Quick Retry (FA/QR)**

These custom implementations are often poorly understood by PS, yielding worse performance/resiliency and complex, hard-to-debug configs. Impact: degraded resiliency/performance and debugging difficulty. Root cause: custom/insufficient FA/QR settings. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Linked tickets: ERE-1341, ERE-1606, ERE-1736, ERE-2623 (escalations). Prevention: better FA/QR defaults and PS guidance (Aha COREREL-19).

**[Story] QR + Preserve-Stale Combination Cached Error Responses (Resolved)**

A customer saw increased edge 504s starting 2024-04-22: an initial 504 from ERR_PURGE_SEQ_OUT_OF_DATE was cached, and ghost then served 504 to subsequent requests without forwarding. Root cause: with 'cache error behavior with stale response = On' + QR, ghost-generated 504s (on purge errors) were saved in memory. Impact: persistent edge 504s served from cache. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - no new escalations or repeat patterns in 2025; KTLO. Workaround: adjust preserve-stale metadata to not save 504s. Linked ticket: ERE-2109. Prevention: disallow the QR + preserve-stale combination that caches error responses (tracked under ERECSO-74).

**[Story] AMD QR Issues - Default percent-to-monitor causes incomplete cached objects (Duplicate)**

The default Quick Retry (QR) percent-to-monitor tag could cause incomplete objects to be delivered/cached, since it makes ghost monitor only part of the object. Impact: object corruption/incomplete cached objects (caused a couple of SIs). Root cause: media default percent-to-monitor setting. Resolution status: Closed / Duplicate - resolved by updating the media default to <percent-to-monitor>100</percent-to-monitor>. Linked tickets: ERE-2211, ERE-2585 (escalations). Prevention: 100% percent-to-monitor default to avoid incomplete-object caching.

**[Story] OIPACL ERR_NON_SUPERNET_IP - Origin requests from non-supernet IPs**

With Origin IP Access Control List (OIPACL) enabled, a ghost not in the supernet allowlist intermittently reaches origin directly, causing ERR_NON_SUPERNET_IP errors. Impact: intermittent origin-request failures for OIPACL-configured customers. Root cause: requests originating from non-supernet IPs under OIPACL setup. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Linked ticket: ERE-2587 (escalation). Prevention: ensure forwarding ghosts stay within the supernet allowlist under OIPACL.

**[Story] Region Overload and Load Misreporting from SNId Configuration (Resolved)**

Platform-wide SNId rollout introduced new problems: SNId requires the correct serial/slot associated with each hostname in control.snid.snitoserial.{essl|freeflow}; hostname discovery (parsing ddc logs) could produce stale/incorrect entries, causing region overload and load misreporting. Impact: region overloads and incorrect load reporting. Root cause: SNId config/hostname-discovery inaccuracies. Resolution status: Closed / Complete - config update frequency increased from weekly to several times daily, and no notable mismatch escalations since. Linked tickets: ERE-2501, ERE-2412, ERE-2599, ERE-2694, ERE-2582 (escalations). Prevention: frequent, accurate SNId config updates.

**[Story] AMD/DD Resiliency Issues - Default media resiliency shortcomings**

Tracks customer escalations due to shortcomings in default media resiliency features such as Quick Retry (QR) and Fail-action (FA). Sub-tasks include ERECSO-116 (QR on ICP path) and ERECSO-117 (QR/SCM mapping). Prevention: strengthen default QR/FA resiliency. No linked ERE tickets at parent level.

**[Story] AMD/DD: QR Inefficiencies on ICP Path**

Sub-task tracking performance issues where Quick Retry (QR) was ineffective because the primary and alternate paths followed the same parent hierarchy. For a cache-miss request (Edge -> TD0/MCH -> CW/Origin), slowness on the shared TD0/MCH parent isn't avoided by QR if the alternate path reuses that same parent. Impact: QR fails to route around parent slowness. Root cause: alternate path sharing the same parent hierarchy. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Parent: ERECSO-115. Linked ticket: ERE-2707 (escalation). Prevention: ensure QR alternate paths use a distinct parent hierarchy.

**[Story] AMD/DD: QR Inefficiencies Due to SCM Mapping**

Sub-task tracking performance escalations where Quick Retry (QR) was ineffective due to the choice of regions on the alternate path (driven by SCM mapping). Impact: QR fails to improve resiliency because alternate-path region selection is sub-optimal. Root cause: SCM mapping choosing poor alternate-path regions. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Parent: ERECSO-115. Linked tickets: ERE-2760, ERE-2974, ERE-2558 (escalations); related to DEL-I-128, MAPPINGENG-60/123, CR 4484696. Prevention: improve alternate-path region selection in SCM mapping.

When machines are temporarily offline for installation (sflag 512 set throughout), they still receive traffic from clients across various hostnames, disrupting end users. Resolution status: Open / Unresolved, workaround available. Linked tickets: ERE-2830, ERE-1374, ERE-2155, ERE-1898, ERE-2756 (escalations).
